_law: FROZEN BENCHMARK BINDING LAW. One COMBINED artifact per semantic card pair: the bound unit pair, the AUTHORITATIVE participant enumeration for each bound unit, the cross-card participant correspondence, and the explicit unbound remainder. It is KEY-SIDE BENCHMARK INSTANTIATION METADATA -- architecture-neutral, candidate-independent, frozen before candidates exist, and NEVER a semantic comparison verdict.
_what: AQ4 combined unit + participant binding schema. Benchmark evaluation law only: it creates no production law, ratifies no architecture, mints no production vocabulary and authorizes no candidate encoder. Production AQ4 architecture remains UNRATIFIED.
status: SCHEMA AND MACHINERY ONLY. No real binding is instantiated: the 354 semantic pairs are not bound, no unit is chosen, and no participant correspondence is adjudicated here.

why_one_artifact._law: Participant correspondence is meaningless without the unit pair it is stated over. Two independently frozen artifacts would create a coherence invariant nobody enforces and a second drift surface.
why_one_artifact.consequence: ONE canonical serialization and ONE artifact hash covering unit binding, participant enumeration and participant correspondence together.

projection_dependency._why: the enumeration's ordinals and canonical anchors are the projection's own participant representation, so the binding is pinned to the version that defines it

record._law: One record per semantic card pair. The card-side order is CANONICAL (ascending oracle_id), so a pair is never stored twice and a direction is never implied by storage.
record.pair: the two oracle_ids in canonical ascending order
record.tranche: the frozen semantic tranche the pair came from

unit_binding._law: The administrative unit-binding law is already frozen and is NOT redesigned here.
unit_binding.not_applicable_law: ADMINISTRATIVE ONLY -- never a semantic disposition, never a comparison verdict, never UNKNOWN or PROVEN-NOT. It records a card case with no valid semantic unit, and a reason is REQUIRED.
unit_binding.null_units: a_unit and b_unit are null exactly when the state is NOT_APPLICABLE for that side

record.a_unit: a four-coordinate occurrence address, or null when administratively not applicable

participant_enumeration._law: AUTHORITATIVE for the future benchmark KEY on the bound unit. The key projection does NOT independently re-enumerate participants: its participant set, anchors and ordinals must MATCH this enumeration exactly, and the repetition there is a derived reference copy required by the projection interface, never a second source of truth.
participant_enumeration.ordinal: integer, and the enumeration's ordinals must be exactly 0..n-1
participant_enumeration.anchor: the canonical RAW_ORACLE anchor, unique within its occurrence, locating that occurrence
participant_enumeration.adjudication: REQUIRED when the source is human; carries the method and status
participant_enumeration.human_additions: A human addition or removal is BENCHMARK INSTANTIATION, not production parser law, and it does not broaden any structural probe.
participant_enumeration.high_risk: multi-participant cases stay in the already-ratified high-risk class and use its independent dual adjudication
participant_enumeration.later_discovery_law: If key fact adjudication later finds a participant missing from a frozen enumeration, do NOT silently renumber and do NOT silently edit the binding. It is a benchmark KEY DEFECT under the existing key-error law and is handled symmetrically there.

participant_binding._law: A PARTIAL ONE-TO-ONE (partial injective) mapping between the two bound units' participants. Each A participant maps to at most one B participant and each B participant to at most one A participant. NO one-to-many or many-to-one correspondence is ratified in v1; a measured case that genuinely needs one is a STOP and returns to Captain.

methods.DETERMINISTIC_SINGLETON: THE ONLY automatic mapping in v1. Precondition: the frozen enumeration of each side has EXACTLY ONE participant; then the unique A participant maps to the unique B participant.
methods.HUMAN_ADJUDICATED: everything else, where a correspondence is required and the singleton rule does not resolve it. Records both canonical anchors, the structural basis, the relevant evidence spans, a CR anchor only where genuinely relied upon, and the adjudication method and status.

participant_binding._why_forbidden: each of those either introduces circularity -- deciding correspondence from the very facts the comparison is about -- or selection bias, or a hidden semantic-role ontology that v1 refuses.
participant_binding.no_alignment_shopping: ONE frozen mapping is reused across every applicable question for that pair. Generating alternate mappings per question, or trying mappings until a desired verdict appears, is forbidden.
participant_binding.disagreement: unresolved adjudicator disagreement stays explicit. A mapping is never forced.

unbound._law: EXPLICIT. Unmapped participants are listed, never inferred from omission.
unbound.unbound_a: enumerated A ordinals carrying no mapping
unbound.reconciliation: the unbound lists must exactly equal the enumerated-but-unmapped ordinals on their side

correspondence_state._law: ADMINISTRATIVE ONLY. These are not semantic dispositions, not PROVEN, not PROVEN-NOT, not UNKNOWN, and not absence claims. When a required correspondence is unavailable the SEMANTIC comparison remains UNKNOWN under its own existing reason class.
correspondence_state.COMPLETE: no enumerated ordinal on either side is left unbound
correspondence_state.PARTIAL: some enumerated ordinal is unbound, and that is recorded rather than resolved
correspondence_state.AMBIGUOUS: adjudication did not settle the correspondence

candidate_fairness._law: Candidate exporters never receive, inspect or alter this artifact.
rules: the key binding and enumeration are frozen before either candidate is implemented
each candidate independently exports its own detected participants with canonical anchors, and projection canonicalization derives the local numbering from those anchors
scoring aligns same-occurrence candidate participants to key participants ONLY through that canonical local representation
a candidate that misses a key participant, invents an extra one, or uses an incompatible anchor degrades or refuses under existing law -- a candidate outcome, never permission to amend the key
candidate documents are validated against the projection schema, never against this artifact

forbidden._law: Each is refused by the validator.
values: a semantic disposition or comparison verdict inside a binding record
a candidate-native field or candidate identity
a semantic role, argument slot, participant kind or global participant id
an automatic mapping other than the singleton rule
a cross-product expansion of the pair population into participant pairs
an alternate mapping generated per question
